implementation_notes: libmicrohttpd hands every request to one MHD_AccessHandlerCallback: read method and url from the connection (MHD_lookup_connection_value), run the shared chain (authentication, logging), then dispatch through a table of {method, pattern, handler} entries and enqueue the answer with MHD_queue_response. What replaces the classic structure: function pointers in a static table replace the FrontController and Command classes, and the common behaviour is a hand-written list of checks called before the dispatch step. Keeping the pattern explicit in C is still justified when a stable ABI and freedom from frameworks matter more than ergonomics.
pitfalls: A return path that answers MHD_YES without queueing a response leaves the request hanging or re-enters the handler; every path must end in MHD_queue_response (or an explicit refusal).
In thread-pool and thread-per-connection modes the callback runs concurrently, so the route table must be immutable after startup and any shared state needs locking.
The url arrives percent-encoded and POST bodies arrive in chunks tracked through *con_cls; parsing them without bounds checks is the classic buffer-overflow site.
libmicrohttpd deliberately ignores most HTTP semantics (methods, ranges, custom headers), so the front controller must implement them uniformly or behaviour diverges per handler.
